rows.text: Under the Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, Article 25(2) and Annex I, Part A, the categories of machinery listed in Annex I, Part A always require one of the Article 25(2) procedures involving a notified body, such as EU type-examination with module C, unit verification (module G), or full quality assurance (module H).

rows.text: For machinery listed in Annex I, Part A, the manufacturer must apply one of the procedures in Article 25(2): module B followed by module C (Annexes VII and VIII), full quality assurance under module H (Annex IX), or unit verification under module G (Annex X).

rows.value: Annex I, Part A, point 5 (safety components with fully or partially self-evolving behaviour).
rows.text: A safety component with fully or partially self-evolving behaviour falls under Annex I, Part A, point 5 of the Regulation. Point 6 covers machinery with embedded self-evolving ML systems, which is a different subject.
Under Annex III, point 1.3.8.1 of the Regulation, guards for moving transmission parts must be interlocking movable guards rather than fixed guards where frequent access is envisaged.

rows.text: Under essential health and safety requirement 1.3.7 of Annex III to the Regulation, the risks addressed are contact leading to hazardous situations, contact that could lead to accidents (where risks persist), moving parts, accidental blockage of moving parts, and psychological stress from interaction with the machinery.

rows.value: The natural or legal person who carries out the substantial modification is treated as the manufacturer under Article 18 of the Machinery Regulation, subject to the Article 10 manufacturer obligations (where the modification affects only the safety of machinery or a related product forming part of an assembly).
rows.text: Under Article 18 of the Machinery Regulation, the natural or legal person carrying out a substantial modification is subject to the manufacturer's obligations in Article 10, provided the modification affects only the safety of that machinery or a related product within an assembly; a non-professional user modifying machinery for own use is excluded.

rows.text: Under Directive 2006/42/EC (Annex I, 1.7.4 and Art. 5(1)), which still applies on 2026-11-14, machinery must be accompanied by instructions in the required language, the instruction manual and the original instructions, and by the EC declaration of conformity. The Regulation's corresponding requirements apply only from 2027-01-20.

The manufacturer must keep the technical documentation and the EU declaration of conformity for at least 10 years, counted from when the machinery or product is placed on the market or put into service (Machinery Regulation, Art. 10(3) and Art. 12(2)).
Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 applies generally from 20 January 2027, as corrected by the corrigendum, although certain Articles apply from earlier dates.
Yes. Directive 2006/42/EC is repealed only from 20 January 2027, and conforming machinery may be placed on the market until then, so 16 January 2027 is still allowed.

The DEMAG overhead travelling crane (IGEA device 8) must be verified once a year (P1Y), under Allegato VII, riga 15, because it is fixed lifting equipment above 200 kg, used in the mining sector, and built in 1985. Assumptions of the rule: truck cranes and mobile cranes are treated as mobile, overhead and gantry cranes and hoists as fixed, and the site's sector applies to every device.

The Effer truck crane at position 7 must be verified every year (P1Y), under the Annex VII rule for mobile lifting equipment above 200 kg used in the extractive sector. Assumptions of the rule: truck cranes and mobile cranes are treated as mobile, overhead and gantry cranes and hoists as fixed, and the site's sector applies to every device.
The periodic verifications after the first one on Annex VII equipment are carried out by the ASL, per DM2011 art. 2 c. 1.

The first periodic verification must be carried out within 45 days of receiving the complete request, under art. 71, c. 11 of Legislative Decree 81/2008. The facts do not support the 60-day figure attributed to the 2011 Ministerial Decree.
No. Under the UR e-Series manual (p. 220), the UR5e may only be put into service once integrated into a final complete machine, since it is partly completed machinery.

The nanoScan3 protective device must be regularly tested at least once a year (nanoScan3 manual, p. 50), and its detection capability test and thorough check of the main function are also required at least once a year (p. 51).
The verifier (aggiudicatario) must give IGEA 15 days' notice when planning the checks, per the igea-equipment document, p. 5.

The IGEA overhead travelling crane at position 13 must be verified every two years, under the Annex VII (D.Lgs. 81/2008) row for fixed lifting equipment in the quarrying sector, built within the last 10 years. Assumptions of the rule: truck cranes and mobile cranes are treated as mobile, overhead and gantry cranes and hoists as fixed, and the site's sector applies to every device.

IGEA device 13 must be verified every P2Y on 2026-11-14: GRU A PONTE SCORREVOLE is lifting equipment of type fisso (mapping of the rule); capacity 5000 kg is above 200 kg; sector estrattivo: named in the row; built in 2017: not more than 10 years before 2026-11-14; Annex VII row for type fisso, sector use, age new. Assumptions of the rule: truck cranes and mobile cranes are treated as mobile, overhead and gantry cranes and hoists as fixed, and the site's sector applies to every device.
